problem_statements.problem_statement: Do the agents with claims match the agent-level early claim rates?
problem_statements.business_intent: Check the supplied agent metric against the claim records.
problem_statements.business_objective: Reconcile Sales_Details.Early Claim Rate against claims actually observed for each agent.
example_queries: Does the early claim rate match the claims data?
Do agent rates agree with claim records?
analytical_steps: Join claims to policies and derive days from inforce to death.
Aggregate observed early claims per SALES_ID over their policy base.
Join Sales_Details to obtain the supplied Early Claim Rate.
Compare the computed rate against the supplied rate per agent.
Report agreement, disagreement and the agents where only one source has data.
State plainly that the two may be measured on different bases.
problem_statements.answer_template: {agreeing} agents agree between computed and supplied early claim rates; {differing} differ.
problem_statements.population: Agents with at least one policy; 134 claims across 1,956 agents.
problem_statements.caveat: Sales_Details rates are supplied aggregates with no stated definition, denominator or measurement window. A mismatch is therefore evidence of a different basis, not necessarily an error in either source. With 134 claims across 1,956 agents, almost every agent has zero observed claims.

calculations: computed early claim rate per agent
evidence_requirements.population_definition: Agents with at least one policy; 134 claims across 1,956 agents.

limitations: Cannot conclude which source is correct; reports divergence only.

problem_statements.problem_statement: Do the five datasets reconcile with each other?
problem_statements.business_intent: Prove the datasets are mutually consistent before trusting any analysis.
problem_statements.business_objective: Run every cross-table reconciliation the schema permits and report the result.

checks.name: every claim resolves to a policy
death-status policies match the claims set exactly
every policy resolves to an agent
every policy resolves to an owner
policy status agrees between Policy and Persistency
renewal paid status matches a present paid date

analytical_steps: Check that every claims AppID exists in Policy_Details.
Check that policies with POLICY.STATUS = 'Death' match the claims set exactly.
Check that POLICY.STATUS agrees between Policy and Persistency on joined rows.
Check that Renewal_Status = 'Paid' is equivalent to a present Renewal_Paid_Date.
Check that every policy SALES_ID exists in Sales_Details.
Identify orphan keys in each direction and report them individually.
Report each check as pass or fail with the exact counts involved.
problem_statements.answer_template: {passed} of {total} reconciliation checks pass; {failed} require attention.
problem_statements.population: All five datasets in full: 25,000 policies, 25,000 owners, 1,956 agents, 134 claims and 24,542 persistency rows.
problem_statements.caveat: The known defect is the single AppID stored as '1.50E+10' in Owner and Persistency (DQ-001), which orphans exactly one policy in each of those two joins. It is reported, not repaired, so the reconciliation reflects the source data as delivered.

evidence_requirements.join_path: all four documented joins plus anti-joins
evidence_requirements.population_definition: All five datasets in full: 25,000 policies, 25,000 owners, 1,956 agents, 134 claims and 24,542 persistency rows.

problem_statements.problem_statement: What data quality issues should I know about?
problem_statements.business_intent: Make the analyst aware of defects before they draw conclusions.
problem_statements.business_objective: Report every recorded data-quality finding with its evidence and impact.
example_queries: What should I be careful about in this data?
analytical_steps: Load the recorded findings from the data contract.
Join the tables named by each finding on their documented keys so the cross-table findings can be re-checked.
Re-verify each finding's evidence counts against the live CSVs.
Report each finding with its severity, affected tables and columns, impact and the handling rule applied.
Flag any finding whose evidence no longer matches, which would mean the data has changed since profiling.
problem_statements.answer_template: {finding_count} data-quality findings are recorded: {high} high, {medium} medium, {low} low severity.
problem_statements.population: All five datasets as profiled in Phase 0, re-verified against the live CSVs at execution time.
problem_statements.caveat: Findings are descriptive. None of the underlying source files is modified by this system.Renewal metrics cover only the Persistency-eligible population, which excludes surrendered and death policies (DQ-006), so they rest on a different denominator from the policy-level figures reported alongside them.

calculations: live re-verification of each finding's counts
evidence_requirements.population_definition: All five datasets as profiled in Phase 0, re-verified against the live CSVs at execution time.

problem_statements.problem_statement: What questions can this data not answer?
problem_statements.business_intent: Set expectations honestly about analytical scope.
problem_statements.business_objective: State the domains the five CSVs cannot support and why.
example_queries: What can't this data tell me?
Which questions are out of scope?
What is missing from the data?
problem_statements.independent_tables: Each table is inspected separately for the presence and cardinality of its own columns. No join is performed because the question is about the schema, not about linked records.
analytical_steps: Load the recorded unanswerable domains from the data contract.
For each, state the missing column or the single-valued column that blocks it.
Verify the blocking evidence against the live data.
Return the list with reasons, so an unsupported question gets a grounded refusal rather than a fabricated answer.
problem_statements.answer_template: {domain_count} analytical domains cannot be supported by these five datasets.
problem_statements.population: The schema of all five datasets rather than their rows: column presence and cardinality determine what is answerable.
problem_statements.caveat: This list is derived from the observed schema. It covers the domains the reference material implied but the data cannot support, including channel comparison, profitability, underwriting and fund performance.

evidence_requirements.population_definition: The schema of all five datasets rather than their rows: column presence and cardinality determine what is answerable.

problem_statements.problem_statement: Is this question something the data can answer?
problem_statements.business_intent: Refuse unsupported questions with a grounded reason instead of guessing.
problem_statements.business_objective: Determine whether a question maps to available columns and explain the gap when it does not.
example_queries: Can you answer questions about profitability?
problem_statements.mentions_unsupported_concepts: This PS exists to refuse unsupported questions. Its example queries name concepts the data lacks on purpose, so the router can be trained to reject them with a grounded reason rather than approximate an answer.
analytical_steps: Extract the concepts the question depends on.
Resolve each concept against the schema, including columns only reachable by a documented join, so a join-only concept is not wrongly refused.
Attempt to map each concept onto an actual column in the data contract.
If every concept maps, route the question to the appropriate PS.
If any concept does not map, identify the missing column or the single-valued column that blocks it.
Return a grounded refusal naming what is missing and, where one exists, the nearest supported question.
problem_statements.answer_template: This question requires {missing_concepts}, which the five datasets do not contain.
problem_statements.population: The schema itself rather than the data rows.
problem_statements.caveat: The correct response to an unsupported question is a grounded refusal that names the missing field. Approximating with a loosely related column would produce a confidently wrong answer, which is the failure mode this PS exists to prevent.Renewal metrics cover only the Persistency-eligible population, which excludes surrendered and death policies (DQ-006), so they rest on a different denominator from the policy-level figures reported alongside them.

columns_used: the concepts that could not be mapped
evidence_requirements.population_definition: The schema itself rather than the data rows.

limitations: Returns a refusal with reasons; performs no data analysis.
